context: Fritha wants a sum of money (in Rand) to grow to a larger target amount over a stated number of whole years in an account that pays simple interest at a fixed annual rate; the rate is unknown and must be found.

params.why: keeps the total growth to a believable size

stem: At what simple interest rate should Fritha invest if she wants to grow $\text{R{=P}}$ to $\text{R{=A}}$ in ${=n}$ years? Give the rate as a percentage per year, written as a number without the % sign.
solution: Read the question and write down the given information: $\begin{aligned}A&=\text{R{=A}}\\P&=\text{R{=P}}\\n&={=n}\\i&=?\end{aligned}$

The question asks for a simple interest rate, so use the simple interest formula $A=P(1+in)$ and make $i$ the subject: $\begin{aligned}A&=P(1+in)\\\frac{A}{P}&=1+in\\\frac{A}{P}-1&=in\\\frac{\frac{A}{P}-1}{n}&=i\end{aligned}$
Write $i$ as a percentage: $i={=idec}\times100={=r}\%$ per year.
So Fritha must invest at a simple interest rate of ${=r}\%$ per annum.
notes: Basic entry point, modelled on we04 (Fritha, R2500 to R4000 in 5 years, 12%). n is given directly, the rate is a whole percent, and every amount is a whole number of Rand: P is a multiple of 100, so gain = (P/100)*r*n is an integer and A = P + gain is exact. The constraint checks that i comes out as exactly r/100. r*n is capped at 90 so total growth stays believable. The answer is the percentage as a plain number (12 for 12%), as the book prints it; the stem says so to keep a blind solver from answering 0.12. No misconceptions are catalogued for this objective and the family is numeric, so there are no distractors.
